draft.title: Regions in the complex plane
card: |z − w| is the distance between the points z and w. So |z − w| = r is a circle with centre w and radius r.
|z − w| < r is the inside of that circle. |z − w| > r is the outside.
|z − a| = |z − b| is the set of points equally far from a and b. It is a straight line, the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them.
Arg(z − w) = θ is a ray starting at w, at angle θ from the positive real direction. Re(z) = k is a vertical line and Im(z) = k is a horizontal line.
draft.remember: Read |z − w| as a distance from w, and Arg(z − w) as a direction from w.

a.q: What does |z − (2 + i)| = 3 describe on the Argand plane?
opts: A circle with centre (2, 1) and radius 3
A circle with centre (−2, −1) and radius 3
A circle with centre (2, 1) and radius 9
A line through (2, 1) at a gradient of 3
a.why: |z − w| = r is a circle with centre w, so the centre is 2 + i, which is (2, 1), and the radius is 3. The sign is not flipped: the centre is w, not −w.
a.clue: Read it as: the distance from z to 2 + i is 3.

opts: The vertical line Re(z) = −1
The vertical line Re(z) = 1
The horizontal line Im(z) = −1
A circle with centre −1 and radius 2
b.why: The equation says z is equally far from 1 and −3. The perpendicular bisector of those two points on the real axis is the vertical line through their midpoint, −1. The midpoint is not 1, which is only one of the points.
b.clue: Write |z + 3| as |z − (−3)|, then find the midpoint of 1 and −3.

a.best: A circle with centre (2, 1) and radius 3

final.title: Regions in the complex plane
card: \(|z - w|\) is the distance between the points \(z\) and \(w\). So \(|z - w| = r\) is a circle with centre \(w\) and radius \(r\).
\(|z - w| < r\) is the inside of that circle. \(|z - w| > r\) is the outside.
\(|z - a| = |z - b|\) is the set of points equally far from \(a\) and \(b\). It is a straight line, the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them.
\(\text{Arg}(z - w) = \theta\) is a ray starting at \(w\), at angle \(\theta\) from the positive real direction. \(\text{Re}(z) = k\) is a vertical line and \(\text{Im}(z) = k\) is a horizontal line.
final.remember: Read \(|z - w|\) as a distance from \(w\), and \(\text{Arg}(z - w)\) as a direction from \(w\).
